title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
summary: Given a string s made up of 'a' and 'b', determine the least deletions required to ensure no 'b' precedes an 'a'.
statement: Given a string s made up of 'a' and 'b', determine the least deletions required to ensure no 'b' precedes an 'a'. A string is balanced if no index i < j exists where s[i] is 'b' and s[j] is 'a'.
constraints: After deletions, every a must precede every b.
hints: At each a, either delete it or delete every b retained before it.
Track preceding b count and the optimal deletions for the processed prefix.
On b increment its count; on a set deletions=min(deletions+1,seen_b).
These are the only two ways to prevent a processed b from remaining before the current a.
editorial: These are the only two ways to prevent a processed b from remaining before the current a.

tests.explanation: Deleting the b at index two and the later a leaves a balanced string using two deletions.
Deleting the first two b characters is optimal.
